name: Animalia
tldr: Multicellular organisms that eat other organisms for energy, most can move, and most develop from an embryo

name: Chordata
tldr: Animals with a spinal cord (or its precursor) at some life stage; includes all vertebrates

name: Arthropoda
tldr: Jointed-leg invertebrates with an exoskeleton; insects, arachnids, crustaceans, myriapods. Most diverse animal phylum by far

name: Mollusca
tldr: Soft-bodied invertebrates, often shelled; snails, clams, squid, octopuses

name: Cnidaria
tldr: Simple aquatic animals with stinging cells; jellyfish, corals, sea anemones

name: Echinodermata
tldr: Marine animals with 5-part radial symmetry as adults; starfish, sea urchins, sea cucumbers

name: Annelida
tldr: Worms built from repeating body segments; earthworms, leeches, marine bristle worms

name: Porifera
tldr: The simplest animals; no true tissues or organs, filter water through pores to feed

name: Mammalia
tldr: Warm-blooded, hairy, feed young on milk. Includes humans, whales, bats, elephants

name: Aves
tldr: Feathered, egg-laying, warm-blooded; most can fly, all evolved from theropod dinosaurs

name: Reptilia
tldr: Cold-blooded, scaled, mostly egg-laying; snakes, lizards, turtles, crocodilians

name: Amphibia
tldr: Cold-blooded, usually water-dependent for reproduction; frogs, salamanders, caecilians

name: Actinopterygii
tldr: Fish with fins supported by bony spines; the vast majority of living fish species

name: Chondrichthyes
tldr: Fish with skeletons made of cartilage, not bone; sharks, rays, skates

name: Insecta
tldr: Six-legged arthropods, usually with wings; over half of all described animal species

name: Arachnida
tldr: Eight-legged arthropods with no antennae; spiders, scorpions, ticks, mites

name: Malacostraca
tldr: The largest crustacean class; crabs, lobsters, shrimp, krill, woodlice

name: Diplopoda
tldr: Arthropods with two pairs of legs per body segment; slow-moving detritivores

name: Primates
tldr: Mammals with forward-facing eyes and grasping hands; monkeys, apes, humans, lemurs

name: Carnivora
tldr: Mammals with specialized shearing teeth; most eat meat, though some (like pandas) don't

name: Cetartiodactyla
tldr: Hoofed mammals with an even number of toes, plus whales and dolphins; they nest inside this same order because whales evolved from a hoofed ancestor

name: Rodentia
tldr: Mammals with continuously growing front teeth for gnawing; over 40% of all mammal species

name: Chiroptera
tldr: The only mammals capable of true, sustained flight

name: Canidae
tldr: Dog-like carnivorans; wolves, foxes, jackals, domestic dogs

name: Felidae
tldr: Obligate carnivores with retractable claws; lions, tigers, domestic cats

name: Ursidae
tldr: Large, mostly omnivorous carnivorans with a stocky build and short tail
